precommitted: This file is committed before any arm is run; changing a threshold after results exist invalidates the comparison.

arms.A: Sonnet direct: one headless session does the whole task.
arms.B: Sonnet orchestrator plus one bounded Haiku worker defined only for the run, pinned to an explicit model id.
arms.C: Diagnostic only: Sonnet orchestrator told to delegate the implementation to the same pinned Haiku worker exactly once. It measures what forced delegation costs; it never feeds the pilot verdict.

oracle_modes.overlay: original test files copied over the result and run in a sandbox
oracle_modes.own_tests: original change touched only tests, so the arm's own tests are run
oracle_modes.review_only: no oracle command; reviewer judgement and scope only

accepted_outcome.note: A failed oracle is never overridden by a model. A reviewer flag 'oracle_coupled' (correct but a name-coupled test fails) only marks the task for human adjudication and counts as not accepted in both arms. A missing, errored or timed-out step is never accepted.

usage_vector.money: UNKNOWN. total_cost_usd from the CLI is a list-price estimate, never a bill; subscription utilization is not exposed per run.
usage_vector.accounting: modelUsage is trusted only if it shows Haiku whenever the main thread called an agent; otherwise the stream's sidechain usage is merged and labelled, and if neither shows it the accounting is 'unverified' and the task cannot support Haiku

decision_rule.task_supports_haiku: accepted in both arms AND arm B recorded an agent call to the pinned worker AND its Haiku usage was captured AND Sonnet tokens in arm B <= arm A for every one of the four kinds
decision_rule.task_inconclusive: anything else with both arms accepted, including no delegation or Haiku usage that could not be captured (accounting unverified)
decision_rule.task_rejects_haiku: arm A accepted; arm B delegated, did not error, and was not accepted. An infrastructure error, timeout or unparseable run in arm B is INCONCLUSIVE, never a rejection
decision_rule.decline_cases: arm B passes (DECLINE_OK) if it made no agent call; delegating at all is DECLINE_FAILED; whether the hard task was also solved is reported, not required; an errored run is inconclusive
decision_rule.promotion: never from a pilot. Fewer than 30 paired tasks cannot show non-inferiority; the provisional 5 percentage-point first-pass margin is evaluated only at 30 or more paired tasks.
decision_rule.task_not_cheaper: accepted in both arms, delegated, and Sonnet tokens in arm B higher than arm A on all four kinds
decision_rule.task_invalid: an arm called an agent other than the pinned worker, Haiku tokens appeared with no recorded agent call, or the stream audit flagged network, path-probing or secret-reaching tool input
decision_rule.pilot_verdict_rules: NO_HAIKU if any decline task delegated or any bounded task rejects Haiku; OPT_IN_CANDIDATE only if every pilot task is scored, at least two bounded tasks all support Haiku, and every decline task passed; anything else INCONCLUSIVE_KEEP_OPT_IN

hard_gates: zero known critical security, data-loss or contract regressions
no edit outside the task's owned scope
a worker never merges, publishes, closes tickets or certifies readiness

isolation.workdir: git archive of the task's base revision into a fresh one-commit repository, so no future history is reachable
isolation.external_writes: none; no Jira, Slack, GitHub write or merge from any arm
isolation.denied_paths: tool-level only: arms may not read, search or write under ~/Bryant-Developments, ~/.claude, /private/tmp/claude-501 or its /tmp/claude-501 alias (merged solutions, oracle tests, transcripts, scratchpads, other arms' workdirs); active workdirs live under /private/var/tmp. Arm-written Python can bypass tool-level rules, so every raw stream is kept next to its record and audited after the fact for network or secret reach and for any absolute path outside the workdir; flagged runs are INVALID. A substring audit is detection, not a boundary.
isolation.oracle_sandbox: agent-authored test code runs under macOS sandbox-exec: no network, no reads of the dev tree or ~/.claude, writes only inside the scratch directory; symlinks resolving outside the scratch copy are removed first
isolation.models: Sonnet and Haiku are pinned by explicit id and the resolved ids are recorded
isolation.settings: --setting-sources local: neither the base repository's .claude/settings.json (hundreds of allow rules, hooks, defaultMode auto) nor personal settings load into an arm. The base repository's CLAUDE.md and the user-level CLAUDE.md still load into both arms equally and are a recorded confound (the latter makes the model type rtk-prefixed commands, hence the plain-command instruction).
isolation.run_order: recorded per run and alternated across tasks because the second arm benefits from a warm prompt cache
isolation.grading: changes and diffs are computed in pure Python against a fresh extract of the base from the trusted repository; git never runs inside an arm's directory, which an arm can write to. Arms may not read or write their own .git.
isolation.preflight: before any run, every oracle must accept the original merged solution (scripts/routing-eval.py preflight)
isolation.oracle_exceptions: t84 only (pinned by a test): oracle_unsandboxed, graded only when the arm's run record exists with no network, secret or outside-workdir flag; reason recorded in the corpus

amendment: Amended three times, the first three before any valid result existed. (1) After independent review of PR 129: verdict semantics, isolation, oracle modes. (2) After two automated security reviews: grading without git in the arm's directory, symlink containment, sandbox read denial. (3) After a first pilot attempt ('run 0') that was stopped part-way because a further independent review found it ran with the base repository's own allow rules and a sandbox that broke one oracle: run 0 is INVALID and its results are not used for any verdict. Changes made after seeing run 0, each driven by a review finding or a measured defect rather than by which arm looked better: project settings no longer load into arms; the scratch session directory is denied; a preflight proves every oracle accepts its known-good merged solution; two task texts now state the exact phrases or function name their oracles assert (t91, t84); t84's oracle runs unsandboxed because sandbox-exec cannot exec the setuid /bin/ps it needs; delegation means a recorded agent call; an infrastructure error never counts as Haiku rejection; decline tasks are judged on the routing decision, not on solving the hard task; diagnostic arm C was added because run 0 showed arm B never delegated. (4) After a corrected pilot had completed (its verdict, INCONCLUSIVE, cannot change under any of these edits because arm B never delegated): the audit was narrowed to network, secret and outside-workdir reach because its first needles (subprocess, os.environ, ~/) flagged ordinary source edits and wrongly marked two tasks INVALID; the /tmp alias was added to the denied paths; raw streams are now retained. Stored flags of the completed pilot were re-filtered through the narrowed set; none of them named network, secret or outside-workdir reach. (5) After the final review of PR 129: sensitive HOME paths denied, relative-traversal and $HOME audit, unsandboxed grading conditional on a clean run record.
